knowledge:
- key_parameters: remove_existing=Set to TRUE to allow overwriting of existing Brick files during creation ;; remove_prior=Set to TRUE to allow overwriting of loaded matrix data inside an existing Brick ;; resolution=The bin size of the Hi-C matrix (e.g., 100000 for 100Kb) ;; distance=Limits the maximum diagonal distance (in bins) to load or plot ;; x_coords=Genomic coordinates for plotting/subsetting, must strictly use ':' as the delimiter (e.g., "chr3R:1:10000000") ;; y_coords=Genomic coordinates for plotting/subsetting, must strictly use ':' as the delimiter ;; norm_factor=Normalization factor to load from mcool (e.g., "Iterative-Correction", or NULL for raw counts) ;; cut_corners=Set to TRUE in rotated plots to truncate TAD boundary lines at the corners
- alternatives: The docs mention using the external 'hic2cool' command-line utility (version > 0.7) to convert '.hic' files to '.mcool' before importing into HiCBricks, and using the 'cooler' command-line tool to convert exported sparse matrices back to '.mcool' format.
- when_to_use: Use this package when handling very large, high-resolution Hi-C datasets that exceed system memory, when calling TADs using the Local Score Differentiator (LSD) algorithm, or when creating publication-quality 1-sample or bipartite (2-sample) heatmaps with TAD annotations.
- pitfalls: HiCBricks will not overwrite existing files or data unless 'remove_existing=TRUE' or 'remove_prior=TRUE' are explicitly passed ;; Human-readable coordinates must strictly use ':' as the delimiter; other delimiters will cause failures ;; Continuous bin tables (where the end of one bin overlaps the start of the next) cause width offsets in GenomicRanges; start coordinates must be offset by +1bp to make the bin table discontinuous before loading ;; 'Brick_return_region_position' may fail if the query region is smaller than a single genomic bin; use 'Brick_fetch_range_index' for finer control ;; In bipartite plots with overlapping TADs, the TAD plotted last will visually obscure any overlapping TADs underneath.

workflows.name: import_from_2d_text
workflows.intent: Create a Brick container and load cis/trans contact matrices from 2D text files.
workflows.stages:
1. Create the project directory and initialize the Brick objects using the bin table with `Create_many_Bricks`.
2. Load the BrickContainer using `load_BrickContainer`.
3. Populate the Brick objects with contact frequencies from the 2D matrix files using `Brick_load_matrix` or `Brick_load_cis_matrix_till_distance`.
workflows.code:
library("HiCBricks")
Bintable_path <- system.file(file.path("extdata", "Bintable_100kb.bins"), package = "HiCBricks")
out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "HiCBricks_vignette_test")
dir.create(out_dir)
Create_many_Bricks(BinTable = Bintable_path, bin_delim=" ", output_directory = out_dir, file_prefix = "HiCBricks_vignette_test", remove_existing=TRUE, experiment_name = "HiCBricks vignette test", resolution = 100000)
BrickContainer_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "HiCBricks_vignette_test")
My_BrickContainer <- load_BrickContainer(project_dir = BrickContainer_dir)
Example_dataset_dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "HiCBricks")
Chromosomes <- c("chr2L", "chr3L", "chr3R", "chrX")
for (chr in Chromosomes) {
    Matrix_file <- file.path(Example_dataset_dir, paste(paste("Sexton2012_yaffetanay_CisTrans_100000_corrected", chr, sep = "_"), "txt.gz", sep = "."))
    Brick_load_matrix(Brick = My_BrickContainer, chr1 = chr, chr2 = chr, resolution = 100000, matrix_file = Matrix_file, delim = " ", remove_prior = TRUE)
}

workflows.name: import_from_sparse_matrix
workflows.intent: Create a Brick container and load contact matrices from sparse 3-column text files.
workflows.stages:
1. Initialize the Brick objects using the discontinuous bin table with `Create_many_Bricks`.
2. Load the sparse matrix data into the Brick objects using `Brick_load_data_from_sparse`.
workflows.code:
Bintable_path <- file.path(sparse_out_dir, "GSE104427_c2c12_40000_abs_discontinuous.bed")
My_sparse_brick_object <- Create_many_Bricks(BinTable = Bintable_path, bin_delim=" ", output_directory = out_dir, file_prefix = "HiCBricks_vignette_test", remove_existing=TRUE, experiment_name = "HiCBricks vignette test", resolution = 40000)
Matrix_path <- file.path(sparse_out_dir, "GSE104427_c2c12_40000_iced_uppertri.matrix")
Load_all_sparse <- Brick_load_data_from_sparse(Brick = My_sparse_brick_object, table_file = Matrix_path, delim = " ", resolution = 40000)

workflows.name: import_from_mcool
workflows.intent: Create a Brick container and load contact matrices directly from an .mcool binary file.
workflows.stages:
1. Initialize the Brick objects directly from the mcool file metadata using `Create_many_Bricks_from_mcool`.
2. Load the BrickContainer using `load_BrickContainer`.
3. Populate the Brick objects with normalized values from the mcool file using `Brick_load_data_from_mcool`.
workflows.code:
Create_many_Bricks_from_mcool(output_directory = out_dir, file_prefix = "mcool_to_Brick_test", mcool = mcool_path, resolution = 10000, experiment_name = "Testing mcool creation", remove_existing = TRUE)
My_BrickContainer <- load_BrickContainer(project_dir = out_dir)
Brick_load_data_from_mcool(Brick = My_BrickContainer, mcool = mcool_path, resolution = 10000, cooler_read_limit = 10000000, matrix_chunk = 2000, remove_prior = TRUE, norm_factor = "Iterative-Correction")

workflows.name: tad_calling_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Call Topologically Associated Domains (TADs) using the LSD algorithm and plot a rotated heatmap with TAD borders.
workflows.stages:
1. Call TADs across chromosomes using `Brick_local_score_differentiator`.
2. Save the called TAD ranges into the Brick container using `Brick_add_ranges`.
3. Retrieve the saved TAD ranges using `Brick_get_ranges`.
4. Define a custom log-transformation function.
5. Plot a 45-degree rotated heatmap with overlaid TAD borders using `Brick_vizart_plot_heatmap`.
workflows.code:
BrickContainer_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "HiCBricks_vignette_test")
My_BrickContainer <- load_BrickContainer(project_dir = BrickContainer_dir)
Chromosome <- c("chr2L", "chr3L", "chr3R", "chrX")
di_window <- 10
lookup_window <- 30
TAD_ranges <- Brick_local_score_differentiator(Brick = My_BrickContainer, chrs = Chromosome, resolution = 100000, di_window = di_window, lookup_window = lookup_window, strict = TRUE, fill_gaps = TRUE, chunk_size = 500)
Name <- paste("LSD", di_window, lookup_window, sep = "_")
Brick_add_ranges(Brick = My_BrickContainer, ranges = TAD_ranges, rangekey = Name, resolution = 100000)
TAD_ranges <- Brick_get_ranges(Brick = My_BrickContainer, rangekey = Name, resolution = 100000)
Failsafe_log10 <- function(x){
    x[is.na(x) | is.nan(x) | is.infinite(x)] <- 0
    return(log10(x+1))
}
Brick_vizart_plot_heatmap(File = file.path(tempdir(), "chr3R-1-10MB-normal-colours-log10-rotate-3-tads.pdf"), Bricks = list(My_BrickContainer), tad_ranges = TAD_ranges, x_coords = "chr3R:1:10000000", y_coords = "chr3R:1:10000000", resolution = 100000, colours = "#230C0F", FUN = Failsafe_log10, value_cap = 0.99, distance = 60, legend_title = "Log10 Hi-C signal", palette = "Reds", width = 15, height = 5, line_width = 0.8, cut_corners = TRUE, rotate = TRUE, return_object=TRUE)
